name: Indo-Pacific Warm Pool
basis: persistent reservoir
summary: The largest persistent expanse of very warm surface water: a continent-like reservoir whose edge moves with threshold, season, and dataset.
inferential_boundary: A warm surface footprint is not a full-depth heat-content integral, and its diagnostic boundary is not a material wall.

name: Western Hemisphere Warm Pool
basis: seasonal reservoir
summary: A seasonally connected warm-water province spanning parts of the tropical eastern Pacific, Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean, and western tropical Atlantic.
inferential_boundary: Central America divides the ocean basins even when a temperature threshold visually joins the warm regions.

name: Northeast Pacific Blob
basis: marine heatwave anomaly
summary: A named marine heatwave demonstrates why a heat blob is an event relative to a baseline—not a permanent ocean province.
inferential_boundary: Its surface expression does not determine its full-depth energy or prove a single cause.

name: El Niño Tongue
basis: basin-scale anomaly
summary: An eastward-reaching equatorial anomaly: a tongue because its geometry and evolution matter as much as its peak temperature.
inferential_boundary: The atlas shape is schematic and is not an event declaration or an ENSO index.

name: Gulf Stream
basis: western boundary current
summary: A narrow, fast pathway that exports warm water poleward and sheds moving rings into the surrounding ocean.
inferential_boundary: Current speed and water temperature do not, by themselves, give heat transport across a section.

name: Kuroshio
basis: western boundary current
summary: The North Pacific counterpart in the map grammar: a swift boundary current, extension, and ring-forming system.
inferential_boundary: The analogy to the Gulf Stream is structural, not an assertion of identical forcing, geometry, or transport.

name: Agulhas System
basis: boundary current / leakage
summary: A current system whose retroflection and rings make exchange look less like a pipe and more like parcels escaping a moving border.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape does not quantify leakage or attribute downstream climate effects.

name: Antarctic Circumpolar Current
basis: fronted zonal current
summary: Earth's clearest ocean belt: a deep-reaching, eastward current whose fronts inhibit exchange while eddies and regional pathways leak heat across them.
inferential_boundary: The ACC is not a solid cold wall and Drake Passage is not a thermal plug.

name: Circumpolar Deep Water
basis: subsurface reservoir / source water
summary: Relatively warm subsurface water can approach Antarctic margins beneath a cold surface, making vertical structure central to ice-shelf exposure.
inferential_boundary: Offshore presence does not equal delivery to a cavity; fronts, shelf breaks, troughs, mixing, and winds intervene.

name: Atlantic Water in the Arctic
basis: subsurface inflow and reservoir
summary: Warm Atlantic-origin water can sit beneath a colder, fresher lid: the Arctic example of why the surface can conceal a large thermal contrast.
inferential_boundary: Subsurface temperature does not determine when, where, or how much heat reaches sea ice or the atmosphere.

name: Drake Passage
basis: circumpolar transport section
summary: The narrowest major gate on the circumpolar route. It makes ACC transport measurable and exposes how geometry reorganizes global circulation.
inferential_boundary: Closing the gate in a model changes many coupled circulations; it is not equivalent to simply sending warm water south.

name: Indonesian Throughflow
basis: inter-basin exchange
summary: A branching tropical gate where land geometry constrains exchange between the Pacific and Indian oceans.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape simplifies multiple straits, vertical structure, tides, mixing, and seasonal reversals.

name: Antarctic Bottom Water
basis: Very cold, dense water formed around Antarctic shelves and margins that spreads into abyssal basins.
summary: The coldest major water mass occupies the deepest layer of much of the world ocean—an immense geography hidden from surface maps.
inferential_boundary: The schematic extent is not its boundary or a claim of uniform properties across every abyssal basin.

name: North Atlantic Deep Water
basis: Relatively salty deep water assembled from northern-source waters and traced by hydrographic properties.
summary: A basin-spanning deep water mass demonstrates that major ocean countries can lie kilometers below the visible surface.
inferential_boundary: Its hydrographic core is modified by mixing and does not define a sealed or uniformly moving parcel.

name: Antarctic Intermediate Water
basis: Cool, relatively fresh Southern Ocean water subducted north of the polar domain and traced at intermediate depth.
summary: A cool, fresh intermediate layer spreads northward beneath warmer surface waters in several basins.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape cannot show its branching cores, mixing, or basin-specific definitions.

name: Subantarctic Mode Water
basis: Thick, weakly stratified water formed by winter mixing north of the Subantarctic Front.
depth: deep winter mixed layer / upper thermocline
summary: A broad Southern Hemisphere mode-water family ventilates the thermocline rather than forming a surface continent.
inferential_boundary: Formation properties and geographic definitions vary by basin and year.

name: North Pacific Intermediate Water
basis: A North Pacific salinity-minimum layer formed and transformed in the subpolar–subtropical transition.
summary: The North Pacific contains a recognizable intermediate layer even where the surface belongs to a warm gyre.
inferential_boundary: The salinity-minimum core is not a fixed-edged body or a direct velocity measurement.

name: Labrador Sea Water
basis: Weakly stratified water renewed by variable deep winter convection in the Labrador Sea.
summary: A named subpolar water mass records formation history and ventilation below the surface.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape does not show variable formation extent or downstream pathways.

name: Mediterranean Outflow Water
basis: Warm, saline Mediterranean-origin water exits Gibraltar and forms an intermediate salinity maximum.
summary: A narrow gate seeds a much larger salty subsurface signature in the Atlantic.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape does not show mixing, meddies, or a measured outflow transport.

name: Red Sea Water
basis: Warm, highly saline water formed by strong evaporation and exported through Bab el-Mandeb.
summary: A small marginal sea leaves a traceable intermediate-water signature far beyond its gate.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape is not the full outflow plume or a transport estimate.

name: North Pacific Subtropical Gyre
basis: A basin-scale wind-driven system of rotating currents surrounding the subtropical interior.
summary: The largest gyre makes an enormous moving province out of water that a heat-only atlas leaves blank.
inferential_boundary: A gyre is a current system, not homogeneous water or a plastic island.

name: South Pacific Subtropical Gyre
basis: A Southern Hemisphere wind-driven current circuit around the subtropical Pacific interior.
summary: A vast circulation realm occupies the South Pacific even without a famous thermal nickname.
inferential_boundary: Its edges shift and do not define a uniform water mass.

name: North Atlantic Subtropical Gyre
basis: A wind-driven current circuit containing the Sargasso Sea and bounded by major currents.
summary: Currents organize the North Atlantic interior into a recognizable rotating realm.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape is not a fixed gyre center or edge.

name: South Atlantic Subtropical Gyre
basis: A wind-driven clockwise current circuit spanning the subtropical South Atlantic.
summary: The basin interior belongs to a circulation system even where no single current line dominates the map.
inferential_boundary: The gyre is variable and internally heterogeneous.

name: Indian Ocean Subtropical Gyre
basis: A Southern Hemisphere wind-driven current circuit shaped by the Indian basin and monsoon influence.
summary: A fifth major subtropical gyre fills much of the Indian Ocean's apparently unlabeled interior.
inferential_boundary: Seasonal monsoon circulation complicates any static outline.

name: Antarctic Polar Front
basis: A circumpolar hydrographic front separating Antarctic and subantarctic waters, with multiple diagnostic definitions.
summary: A front gives the Southern Ocean an edge, but it meanders, branches, and leaks rather than forming a wall.
inferential_boundary: The schematic line cannot represent the front's changing circumpolar path.

name: Subantarctic Front
basis: A major ACC-associated front bounding the Polar Frontal Zone to the north.
summary: Another circumpolar edge shows why the Southern Ocean is a stack of belts rather than one cold ring.
inferential_boundary: Its surface expression can be weak and its position varies regionally.

name: Equatorial Pacific Divergence
basis: Wind-driven divergence draws cooler, nutrient-rich subsurface water toward the equatorial surface.
summary: Some ocean geography is a seam where water rises, not a mass sitting still.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape does not diagnose upwelling rate or the changing cold-tongue footprint.

name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge
basis: A long volcanic ridge formed at a divergent plate boundary along the Atlantic basin floor.
summary: The Atlantic has a mountain spine beneath the water that helps organize basins and deep pathways.
inferential_boundary: A single point cannot show ridge segmentation, transform faults, or water-column effects.

name: East Pacific Rise
basis: A fast-spreading mid-ocean ridge system forming new Pacific seafloor.
summary: A second submerged mountain system gives the Pacific a hidden structural spine.
inferential_boundary: The point is only an index to a long segmented ridge system.

name: Mariana Trench
basis: A very deep, narrow depression formed where one tectonic plate subducts beneath another.
summary: The deepest ocean geography is a hadal trench—not a surface color or current.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape does not represent the trench's full arc or habitat variability.

name: Kerguelen Plateau
basis: A broad elevated seafloor province in the southern Indian Ocean that steers deep and circumpolar flows.
depth: seabed; rises into deep water column
summary: Submerged plateaus can redirect fronts and currents even though they are invisible at the surface.
inferential_boundary: The point does not quantify bathymetric steering or delimit the plateau.

name: Eastern Tropical North Pacific OMZ
basis: A persistent subsurface region where oxygen consumption and weak ventilation maintain low concentrations.
summary: A vast subsurface oxygen geography exists beneath tropical surface waters.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape is not a hypoxia threshold contour, habitat forecast, or current measurement.

name: Eastern Tropical South Pacific OMZ
basis: Low ventilation and biogeochemical oxygen consumption sustain a major eastern tropical subsurface minimum.
summary: The southeast Pacific contains a major low-oxygen province layered beneath productive surface waters.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape does not encode oxygen concentration, threshold, or vertical extent.

name: Arabian Sea OMZ
basis: High productivity, respiration, stratification, and circulation combine to maintain low subsurface oxygen.
summary: The Arabian Sea is a named chemical province as well as a geographic sea.
inferential_boundary: The point is not an oxygen contour and does not imply uniform ecological effects.

name: Sargasso Sea
basis: A clear, nutrient-limited ecosystem within the North Atlantic subtropical gyre, bounded by currents rather than land.
summary: The Sargasso Sea proves that an ocean sea can be geographically real without a coastline.
inferential_boundary: The schematic shape does not delimit a fixed ecosystem boundary or uniform productivity.
